card.occupation: Part-time office administrator at a scaffolding and skip-hire firm's yard office in Rainham, about 24 hours a week across Monday to Thursday. He answers the phone, books in skip drop-offs and collections, chases unpaid invoices, and keeps the drivers' timesheets.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 in 1989 with a handful of GCSEs, including a C in maths and a D in English. He started a YTS scheme in a warehouse and didn't finish it. He has no formal qualifications since then, apart from a forklift ticket that has long since lapsed and a one-day health and safety course the firm sent him on.
card.household: Lives with his wife Tracey, 50, a healthcare assistant on a hospital ward, in an ex-council three-bed terrace they bought under Right to Buy in the late nineties. Their son Liam, 26, moved out two years ago and rents a flat in Romford with his girlfriend. They have no pets since the dog died.
card.cultural_background: White British. Born and raised in Dagenham to a family with roots in the East End. His dad worked at the Ford plant, and his mum did cleaning jobs. He has no religion and doesn't think about it. He is the sort of East London that moved out to Essex-side estates a generation ago and stayed. He has watched the area change and has opinions about it, but mostly he complains about rents, parking and the council.
card.professional_persona: Does what the job needs and not much more. He moved into the office side eight years ago after his back stopped him doing yard work, and he quietly prefers being indoors with the kettle. He is good on the phone with the regular trade customers and blunt to the point of rude with anyone new or awkward. He lets filing pile up and does it in bursts when the boss moans. He is not above rounding his hours up, or 'forgetting' to log a cash job so a driver owes him a favour.
card.sports_persona: West Ham fan by inheritance. He had a season ticket at Upton Park but gave it up after the move to the London Stadium, which he still calls a 'soulless bowl'. Now he watches on the telly, usually through a dodgy stream on the laptop. He doesn't play anything. His exercise is walking to the shop and back.
card.arts_persona: Not interested and doesn't pretend to be. He watches quiz shows, the odd Netflix crime series Tracey puts on, and old episodes of Only Fools and Horses. He hasn't been to a theatre since a school trip and sees no reason to go.
card.travel_persona: Same thing most years: a week in Tenerife or the Algarve, all-inclusive, booked by Tracey. He also does the occasional weekend at a caravan park in Clacton. He has a passport but no curiosity about anywhere he can't get a full English. He is complaining about the price of flights and airport parking before they've even left.
card.culinary_persona: Meat-and-two-veg man. Dinner is whatever Tracey cooks or a takeaway on Friday, usually Chinese or a kebab. He can do a fry-up and beans on toast and that's his range. He drinks tea with two sugars, and a few cans of lager watching the football.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching West Ham on the telly
Doing paid online surveys and studies for a bit of extra cash
Scratchcards and the odd accumulator bet on a Saturday
Messing about on Facebook Marketplace, buying and flipping bits of tools and gear
Pub quiz at the local once a month if Tracey drags him
skills: Knows the local trade customers and roads well enough to quote a skip delivery off the top of his head
Basic spreadsheet and invoicing software, self-taught
Persistent at chasing late payers on the phone
Can haggle anyone down on Marketplace
Can drive pretty much anything with wheels
card.career_goals: Honestly none. He wants to keep his hours steady, avoid being asked to do more, and get to state pension age with as little hassle as possible. He'd take more money for the same work if it was going, and he keeps an eye out for any cash-in-hand side earners.
card.voice: London accent, East End by way of Dagenham, but not stage cockney. He drops some t's and h's and says 'mate' a lot. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal and now and then 'you was'. His answers are short and flat, sometimes a single 'yeah' or 'not really'. He hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm' and uses 'sort of' when he can't be bothered to be precise. He doesn't fill silences. He'll just wait, or say 'that it?' to move things on. He gets a bit more talkative and sarcastic if the subject is money, the council or football.
card.typing: All lower case, no full stops at the end, the odd comma. He drops apostrophes ('dont', 'its', 'cant'). Answers are short, often a few words, with occasional typos he doesn't fix. He uses 'n/a' or 'dunno' if a question bores him, and sometimes 'ok' or 'yes' when a sentence was asked for.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit curt. He gives the impression he's doing you a favour by being there, and he's clear that it's for the money. He isn't openly hostile but is quick to say if a question seems pointless or nosy. He warms up a bit if you let him moan about something, but stays wary of being judged.
small_things: The price of parking at the hospital where Tracey works
Someone on the street nicking his parking space again
West Ham's latest manager being useless
The firm's van getting another ULEZ fine
A Marketplace bloke who tried to mug him off on a price
His back playing up if he sits too long
deeper_things: He resents that his dad had a proper job at Ford for life and he never had anything like it
He feels a bit pushed out since Liam moved in with his girlfriend and rarely rings
He hasn't got much saved and worries quietly about what retirement will look like
He fell out with his younger brother over their mum's house after she died and they haven't spoken in four years
He knows Tracey earns more and works harder than him and it niggles at him
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below face height and angled up, so the shot shows a lot of chin and ceiling. Lit by a warm overhead ceiling light plus the screen glow, with some shadow under the eyes. A heavy-set white man in his early fifties with a round, ruddy face, a day's grey stubble, and short greying brown hair clipped close at the sides and thinning on top. Neutral, slightly unimpressed expression, mouth closed, looking just off to the side of the camera. No glasses. He wears a navy zip-up fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a younger man in a graduation-style gown, a wall clock, and the edge of a doorway into a small kitchen with a white fridge-freezer covered in magnets. A corner of a grey fabric sofa with a West Ham cushion is visible to the left.
